newsitem.title: USA: Amoco EPS boosted by higher energy prices.
newsitem.headline: Amoco EPS boosted by higher energy prices.

text.p: Amoco Corp, reporting record earnings for the nine months, cited higher energy prices, which were partly offset by lower chemical and petroleum products margins.
Nine-month earnings rose to $1.96 billion or $3.95 per share from $1.66 billion or $3.34 per share a year ago.
Third-quarter earnings of $635 million or $1.28 per share included a gain of $97 million on the sale of the company's polystyrene foam products business.
Amoco said worldwide capital and exploration expenditures rose to $3.10 billion in the first nine months of 1996.
It said this compares with $2.75 billion for the same 1995 period and reflects planned spending increases in growth areas.

It said U.S. exploration and production operations earned $224 million in the quarter, up from $159 million a year earlier. The rise was due mostly to higher crude and natural gas prices and increased natural gas volumes, partly offset by higher exploration expenses.

Amoco's U.S. natural gas prices averaged about $1.70 per thousand cubic feet (mcf) during the quarter, about $0.50 per mcf higher than the 1995 third quarter. Average crude oil prices were up about $4.70 per barrel and averaged about $20.55 per barrel.
Natural gas production increased four percent with the third quarter of 1995. Third-quarter 1996 crude oil and natural gas liquids (NGL) production also increased four percent from a year ago.
Canadian operations, which include supply and marketing of NGL, earned $35 million in the quarter compared to a loss of $10 million in the same prior year period.
Overseas exploration and production operations earned $104 million in the quarter, up from the $91 million reported in the 1995 period.

"Third-quarter 1996 performance was below the year-earlier period as lower downstream margins more than offset strong exploration and production results worldwide," said chairman H. laurance Fuller in a statement.

Amoco said petroleum products operations earnings fell to $92 million from $131 million in the quarter as lower refining margins, reflecting higher crude oil costs, more than offset gains associated with asset dispositions. Third-quarter 1996 earnings fell from those for the 1995 period as lower refining margins more than offset gains from asset dispositions.

In chemicals, excluding the one-time gain, earnings in the third quarter were $120 million compared with $296 million in the 1995 same period. Current-quarter results were hurt by lower margins. Industry-wide inventory destocking early in the year accelerated the reduction in margins.
